name: g_stateSequence62Vtable
comment: Vtable of the std_StateSequence62 animation state machine (7 words: a null complete-destructor slot, the delete stub 0x006C7B4C, then std_StateSequence62_Tick/ChangeState/SetState and two more overrides). maybe_Action_Subclass4Anim_Ctor installs it in the state-sequence member at action+0x2C; callers dispatch it at +0x10 and +0x14.
evidence: Literal 0x002C09AC in maybe_Action_Subclass4Anim_Ctor (0x002C074C) stores it at self+0x2C. The two null words at 0x0075AB08/0x0075AB0C are the next table's header (next vptr 0x0075AB10), so this table is exactly 7 words ending at 0x0075AB04; structs.json class std_StateSequence62 lists the code part 0x0075AAF0 with 6 slots (std_StateSequence62_Tick 0x006C7A58, ChangeState 0x006C7834, SetState 0x006C7B14) and 0x006C7A58 itself calls vptr+0x10.

name: g_flwActionVtable
comment: Vtable of the small 44-byte (0x2C) action descriptor built by maybe_Action_InstallVtable for slot 5 of a field actor's action table, the entry tagged "flw" (meaning not known). Word 0 is 0, word 1 the deleting destructor 0x00294928, words 2-4 are stubs and the only real method is maybe_Anim_SyncActorPosition, which copies the owning actor's position into the animator each frame.
evidence: Only literal 0x00294924, in maybe_Action_InstallVtable (0x002948FC); its sole caller maybe_Actor_CreateActionTable (0x0022AF9C) allocates 0x2C bytes, passes the .text string "flw" (0x0022B4B4, in the action/nut/flw/run/slip/fall/get_off_vehicle blob) and Container_SlotReplace's the result into slot 5. The installer forwards to Actor_Action_InitDescriptor (0x00294BD4, base table 0x0075DD00) and then overwrites word 0 with this table: 0x00294928 (calls 0x00193E44 then operator delete), 0x002948F4 and 0x002948F8 and 0x00294BCC are 'bx lr', 0x00294894 is maybe_Anim_SyncActorPosition, then the shared tail 0x00193CD8/0x00193CD4/0x0062A704/0x0062A714/0x0062A70C.

name: g_followTaskVtable
comment: Vtable of the 0x58-byte behaviour task whose action name is "follow": every constructor that allocates it passes that string. maybe_Action_Ctor installs it; words 2-5 are Battle_Action_EvaluateBlendWeights, a forwarder to a virtual of the owner at +0x28, maybe_Action_CheckAnimationMode and Battle_Action_UpdateClipTiming, and Monster_UpdateBehavior swaps in the sibling table 0x0076DEFC, which only changes word 1.
evidence: Only literal 0x00294B90, in maybe_Action_Ctor (0x00294B48). All three BL callers allocate 0x58 and pass the string "follow" (0x0022FEE8): Actor_CreateBehaviourTasks 0x0022FDC8, Monster_UpdateBehavior 0x00232660 and the big container routine at 0x0022E494 (reported as Model_AttachAccessoriesAndWeapons) at 0x0022E6D0. Monster_UpdateBehavior then stores 0x0076DEFC at obj[0] (same words 2-10, different word 1). Words: 0x00294BB8 complete dtor (installs this table, b 0x00294C88), 0x00294B9C deleting dtor, 0x00294A00, 0x00294B2C, 0x00294AFC, 0x00294938, then 0x00193CD8/0x00193CD4/0x0063A8B8/0x0062A714/0x0062A70C. structs.json maps this table to class Battle_Action, but the real Battle_Action vtable is 0x00763978 (named by G_004), so that class link is a mis-assignment.

name: g_actionBaseVtable
comment: Vtable of the common action base class between Gfx_ObjectDesc and the concrete action classes: maybe_Action_CtorBase installs it and 50 constructors (field actions, monster behaviours, gimmicks) run it first. Words 0/1 are its destructor pair (0x00294C88 just branches to the Gfx_ObjectDesc destructor body 0x00193E44), words 2-4 are 'bx lr' no-ops and words 5-10 are the shared object-descriptor slots.
evidence: Only literal 0x00294C70, in maybe_Action_CtorBase (0x00294C34), which calls maybe_Gfx_ObjectDesc_Init with flags|0x20000001 and stores arg2 at obj[10]; 50 BL callers. 0x00294C88 is 'b 0x00193E44', 0x00294C74 is 'bl 0x00193E44; pop; b 0x0010F6CC' (deleting dtor), 0x00294C28/0x00294C30/0x00294C2C are E12FFF1E 'bx lr'. Tail 0x00193C6C/0x00193CD8/0x00193CD4/0x0063A8B8/0x0062A714/0x0062A70C is the generic object-descriptor tail; words 5, 6, 9 and 10 are identical to Gfx_ObjectDesc's own table 0x00758E70, while word 7 (0x00193CD4) and word 8 (0x0063A8B8) replace that table's 0x0019C898/0x0062A704. Battle_Action's table 0x0075DCCC overrides exactly words 2-5 of this one. No structs.json class claims this vtable.

name: g_actionSubclass4AnimVtable
comment: Vtable of the action subclass built by maybe_Action_Subclass4Anim_Ctor: a 0x114-byte action object with an animation state sequence at +0x2C and four 0x18-byte animation refs at +0x50. Word 1 is the deleting destructor thunk; words 2-22 are the move-action handlers (UpdateAnimStep0, Detach, UpdateAnimation, AdvanceState, ReleaseObject, RestorePosition, InterpolateToTarget, FinishLanding ...), and the destructor at 0x002C09F4 writes this address back before freeing.
evidence: maybe_Action_Subclass4Anim_Ctor (0x002C074C) stores literal 0x002C09A8 at obj[0] (after maybe_Action_CtorBase) and literal 0x002C09AC (0x0075AAEC, the state-sequence table) at obj+0x2C, then builds four 0x18-byte anim refs at obj+0x50; its only caller allocates 0x114 bytes. The deleting destructor maybe_Actor_Action_DtorDeleteC (0x002C09F4) re-loads it from literal 0x002C0A10. Slots: 0 null, 1 0x002C09F0, 2 maybe_Actor_Action_Move_UpdateAnimStep0, 3 maybe_Actor_Action_Detach, 4 maybe_Actor_Action_Move_UpdateAnimation, 7 Move_AdvanceState, 11 ReleaseObject, 12 Move_RestorePosition, 13 InterpolateToTarget, 14 UpdateBankingTilt, 22 FinishLanding. structs.json lists the code part 0x0075FD00 (22 slots) under Actor_Action and owns the ctor under class Action_Subclass4Anim; the next table starts at 0x0075FD60, so this one is 23 words.
